title: Tiered stochastic reserve for prefill/decode
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Long-tail latency during prefill/decode remains the dominant cause of SLA misses for medium-sized tenants. Existing deterministic phase-splitting and strict token-reservation policies either underutilize GPU kernels (hurting throughput) or overcommit headroom (hurting fairness).

Proposal: Implement a 'tiered stochastic reserve' allocator that probabilistically reserves micro-slices of compute capacity for higher-priority tenants while allowing opportunistic reclamation by lower-priority workloads. The allocator operates at the phase-split boundary (prefill vs decode) and integrates kernel-selection signals and attention-density hints to decide whether to commit a reserve for the upcoming slice. Reserves are weighted by tenant priority tier and tuned via a decay parameter to avoid starvation.

Goals: reduce 99.9th percentile latency for P0/P1 tenants by 20% while preserving aggregate throughput within -5% of baseline and keeping fairness (measured as median slowdown across tenants) within 10% of current behavior.
background:
Current schedulers use either deterministic slices (fixed window reservation) or full auction-based priority. Deterministic slices are predictable but rigid; auction systems are flexible but introduce head-of-line blocking and unpredictable microburst behavior. Kernel-selection signals (e.g., attention density, kv cache size, sequence length) provide an early indicator of compute cost, but are not currently fused into reservation policy.

This ticket explores a middle ground: probabilistic reservation informed by kernel-cost predictions and attention heuristics, combined with a lightweight reclaim path and kernel-aware packing to preserve throughput.
design_decisions:
1) Reservation granularity: micro-slices sized to roughly 50-200 tokens-equivalent (configurable).
2) Probability model: per-tier base reservation probability p_t, modulated by predicted kernel cost C (higher C => lower p to avoid waste) and recent reclaim rate R (higher R => increase p for stability).
3) Decay/lease: reserved slices have a short lease (measured in scheduling ticks) and a decay that reduces held headroom if not used.
4) Reclaim strategy: optimistic reclaim where lower-priority microbatches can be preempted on kernel-availability signals; preemption uses graceful backoff (hedged reissue to alternate model variant) to avoid failed requests.
5) Kernel hints: scheduler queries kernel estimator (attention density, kv cache size, quantization path) for a predicted cost score. Reserve decisions use a sigmoid mapping from cost to effective probability.
6) Fairness accounting: track per-tenant effective throughput and latency, and enforce a soft token-quota if long-term drift exceeds threshold.
7) Feature flag: gate initial rollout behind runtime.feature.stochastic_reserve and a per-cluster tuning params set.
implementation_notes:
- Add new allocator module: tiered_stochastic_reserve.{rs,py} with a pluggable probability function.
- Extend kernel_cost_estimator RPC to return attention_density_score and kv_state_estimate for prefill.
- Integrate early-exit path so reserve decisions occur before kernel selection commit to avoid extra kernel churn.
- Metrics: reserve_granted, reserve_reclaimed, reserve_utilization, reserved_percentile_latency_by_tier, reclaimed_preemption_rate.
- Add unit tests for probability calibration and deterministic seed runs.
- Add integration test with local runtime harness to simulate mixed tenants and microburst traffic.
- Update SDK docs: note new feature flag and configuration knobs for enterprise tenants.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end experiment shows >=15% reduction in 99.9p latency for P0 tenants in mixed workload bench (target 20% ideal).
2) Aggregate throughput reduction must be <=5% vs baseline in the same bench.
3) Reclaim/preemption failure rate <0.5% of requests (graceful handoffs count as success).
4) No regression in 50p latency for low-priority tenants beyond 25% from baseline.
5) Logs and metrics must provide traceability for every reserved slice (request id -> reserve id).
6) Rollout plan documented and feature-flagged per-cluster.
metrics_and_dashboards:
- New dashboard: Stochastic Reserve — includes reserve_granted_rate, reserve_utilization, reserve_reclaim_rate, p99/p999 latency by tenant tier, throughput delta vs baseline.
- Add alert: reserve_reclaim_rate > 2% sustained for 5m -> investigate kernel mismatch or miscalibration.
- Add alert: p999 latency for P0 increases >10% after enablement -> auto-disable feature in cluster.
- Tag traces with reserve_id to correlate with kernel selection logs in console.
rollout_plan:
1) Unit tests + integration harness locally (dev cluster).
2) Canary in a single soft-quota cluster with synthetic mixed tenants (1% traffic).
3) Run 72-hour experiment with A/B traffic split vs baseline; record metrics.
4) Gradual ramp (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with manual checkpoints and automated rollback if alerts trigger.
5) Post-rollout: tune per-tier p_t values and decay parameter based on observed reclaim/utilization.
6) Bake into runtime-2.4 after stable 7-day window.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-reserving leads to lower cluster throughput and increased cost. Mitigation: conservative default p_t values, fast decay, automatic reclaim path, and short canary window.
Risk: Kernel-cost estimator mispredictions cause misallocation. Mitigation: keep probabilistic model conservative for high predicted-cost requests and backfill with opportunistic packing. Add telemetry to detect estimator bias.
Risk: Starvation of low-priority tenants during sustained bursts. Mitigation: implement soft token-quota and long-term fairness correction every X minutes.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for probability function determinism and edge cases.
- Integration test: mixed-tenant harness with synthetic attention-density patterns to verify reserve grant/reclaim flows.
- Load experiments: compare baseline scheduler vs stochastic reserve under three workload shapes: steady, microburst, and attention-heavy (long context).
- Chaos test: force kernel selection delays to validate graceful reclaim and hedged fallback behavior.
- Long-run fairness test: measure 24h tenant throughput drift and ensure soft-quota enforcement works.
